name: Acousticon electrical hearing aid
description: The Hutchison Acoustic Company listed the Acousticon as an instrument for deaf people at the St. Louis exposition in 1904.

impact.note: An early commercial electrical hearing aid, read as the arrival of that device class, giving modest help to deaf users and leading to later aids.

date.basis: Date applies to this specific event or witness, not global invention.

events.statement: The Hutchison Acoustic Company listed the Acousticon as an instrument for deaf people at the St. Louis exposition in 1904.

evidence.supports: The 1904 guide lists Hutchison Acoustic Company’s Acousticon and Massacon as instruments for deaf people. Exhibition does not prove sales or individual effects.
The historian describes Hutchison’s battery-powered Acousticon and 1903 promotions while critically examining the framing of deaf people; promotion does not establish universal benefit.

events.caveats: The fair guide lists an exhibit and does not show purchase or individual effectiveness. A historian critically examines the period’s framing of deaf people; earlier acoustic and electrical devices existed.
